## Launch {.unnumbered}

This individual Main Mission follows Power Circuits Questions 1-6. Provide a powered-off desktop, the repository cutaway and power schematic, exterior PSU nameplate access, calculator, and the editable Google Doc. Students do not install an OS or alter hardware.

## Functional answers {.unnumbered}

- **Parallel loads:** branches receive the intended rail voltage and operate without forcing all load current through one series path.
- **Power button:** it normally sends a low-power control signal to motherboard power-management logic.
- **Sealed PSU:** hazardous stored energy and mains-connected parts can remain inside. No student opening or energized probing is permitted.
- **Nameplate:** the wattage is a maximum rated capacity under stated conditions, not a measurement of present consumption.

## Calculation answers {.unnumbered}

### Question 2 {.unnumbered}

\answer{$P_1=V_1I_1=(12.0\ \mathrm{V})(0.460\ \mathrm{A})=5.52000\ \mathrm{W}\approx5.52\ \mathrm{W}$.}

::: {.tejwarning title="Significant figures"}
Both measured values have three significant figures, so the multiplication result is reported as $5.52\ \mathrm{W}$, three significant figures.
:::

### Question 3 {.unnumbered}

\answer{$I_2=\dfrac{P_2}{V_2}=\dfrac{7.50\ \mathrm{W}}{5.00\ \mathrm{V}}=1.50000\ \mathrm{A}\approx1.50\ \mathrm{A}$.}

::: {.tejwarning title="Significant figures"}
$P_2$ and $V_2$ each have three significant figures, so $I_2$ is reported as $1.50\ \mathrm{A}$.
:::

### Question 4 {.unnumbered}

\answer{$R_2=\dfrac{V_2}{I_2}=\dfrac{5.00\ \mathrm{V}}{1.50\ \mathrm{A}}=3.33333\ldots\ \Omega\approx3.33\ \Omega$.}

::: {.tejwarning title="Significant figures"}
The inputs each carry three significant figures, so $R_2$ is reported as $3.33\ \Omega$.
:::

### Question 5 {.unnumbered}

\answer{$P_T=5.52\ \mathrm{W}+7.50\ \mathrm{W}+42.0\ \mathrm{W}+18.6\ \mathrm{W}=73.62\ \mathrm{W}\approx73.6\ \mathrm{W}$.}

::: {.tejwarning title="Decimal-place rule"}
For addition, round to the least precise decimal place. The $42.0\ \mathrm{W}$ and $18.6\ \mathrm{W}$ values limit the sum to one decimal place, so the answer is $73.6\ \mathrm{W}$.
:::

### Question 6 {.unnumbered}

\answer{$73.6\ \mathrm{W}$ is below the $400\ \mathrm{W}$ rating by $326.4\ \mathrm{W}$. The rating describes PSU capacity, while actual load varies with operating state, efficiency, and connected components.}

::: {.tejwarning title="Precision note"}
The comparison may be stated to one decimal place because $P_T$ is known to one decimal place. Do not present the nameplate rating as a live power measurement.
:::

## Assessment check {.unnumbered}

Look for accurate labels, complete GUESS steps, equations before substitution, units on every value, full calculator results before rounding, correct final precision, answer sentences, a safe inspection, and a reflection that connects parallel branches and PSU capacity to the real computer.

## Google Classroom posting {.unnumbered}

**Topic:** Main Assignments

**Title:** Computer Power and Parts Mission

Make one copy for each student. Students submit the completed Google Doc, labelled image, six responses, GUESS work, final-answer table, and reflection.
